strings.d1.s0.name: Nyhavn
strings.d1.s0.tips: Colourful 17th-century harbour. Andersen lived at No. 20. Quiet in the morning, and canal tours depart from here.
strings.d1.s1.name: Canal Tour Copenhagen
strings.d1.s1.tips: One-hour canal tour (Stromma or the cheaper Netto). See the Little Mermaid from the water, plus the Opera House and Christianshavn.
strings.d1.s2.name: Amalienborg Palace
strings.d1.s2.tips: The royal residence. The changing of the guard is at 12:00, and the Marble Church dome is nearby.
strings.d1.s3.name: Torvehallerne
strings.d1.s3.tips: Glass market at Nørreport: Hallernes smørrebrød (open sandwich), Grød porridge and Coffee Collective.
strings.d1.s4.name: Round Tower
strings.d1.s4.tips: Round tower from 1642 with a spiral ramp and views over the city.
strings.d1.b0.name: Schønnemann
strings.d1.b0.tips: A smørrebrød institution since 1877. Book ahead; try the herring and schnapps.
strings.d1.b1.name: Designmuseum Danmark
strings.d1.b1.tips: Corridor of Danish design chairs. An alternative to the Round Tower.
strings.d2.s0.name: Rosenborg Castle
strings.d2.s0.tips: Renaissance castle with the Crown Jewels in the basement, set beside the King's Garden.
strings.d2.s1.name: Kongens Have
strings.d2.s1.tips: A winter stroll through the gardens.
strings.d2.s2.name: Statens Museum for Kunst
strings.d2.s2.tips: The national gallery: Matisse and the Danish Golden Age.
strings.d2.s3.name: Aamanns 1921
strings.d2.s4.name: Tivoli Gardens
strings.d2.s4.tips: Amusement park and gardens from 1843, said to have inspired Disney. Lights in the evening and free summer concerts on Fridays. Entry is 175 plus a ride ticket. In winter it runs Christmas and Halloween seasons.
strings.d2.b0.name: Tivoli Food Hall
strings.d2.b0.tips: Food hall next to the park. No entry ticket needed.
strings.d2.b1.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
strings.d2.b1.tips: Rodin, Gauguin and a winter garden. An alternative to SMK, and free on Tuesdays.
strings.d3.s0.name: Church of Our Saviour
strings.d3.s0.tips: Tower with an external spiral staircase of 400 steps, overlooking the Christianshavn canals.
strings.d3.s1.name: Freetown Christiania
strings.d3.s1.tips: Hippie autonomous district founded in 1971. Pusher Street was closed (2024). Follow the photo rule. Cafes and Grå Hal.
strings.d3.s2.name: Reffen Street Food
strings.d3.s2.tips: Reffen is closed in winter. Go to Broens Gadekøkken (under the bridge) or La Banchina instead.
strings.d3.s3.name: Copenhagen Opera House
strings.d3.s3.tips: Henning Larsen's opera house on Holmen. See it from the outside.
strings.d3.s4.name: Copenhill Amager Bakke
strings.d3.s4.tips: Ski slope and walking trail on the roof of a waste-to-energy plant. The city views are free.
strings.d3.b0.name: Christianshavns Bådudlejning
strings.d3.b0.tips: Cafe on the canal, with boat hire.
strings.d3.b1.name: Danish Architecture Center BLOX
strings.d3.b1.tips: Architecture centre with a slide. An alternative to Copenhill.
strings.d4.s0.name: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
strings.d4.s0.tips: 35 minutes by train (Humlebæk). Giacometti, Kusama and a sculpture garden overlooking the Øresund, among the world's most beautiful museums.
strings.d4.s1.name: Louisiana Café
strings.d4.s1.tips: Museum cafe with sea views and a smørrebrød buffet.
strings.d4.s2.name: Kronborg Castle
strings.d4.s2.tips: In Helsingør: Hamlet's Elsinore, with Holger Danske in the casemates and the Swedish coast across the water.
strings.d4.s3.name: Helsingør Old Town
strings.d4.s3.tips: Medieval streets and the Maritime Museum (BIG). Take the train back.
strings.d4.b0.name: Brasserie Kronborg
strings.d4.b0.tips: On Helsingør harbour, beside the castle.
strings.d4.b1.name: Karen Blixen Museum Rungstedlund
strings.d4.b1.tips: Home of the author of Out of Africa. On the way to Louisiana, as an alternative to Kronborg.
strings.d5.s0.name: Carlsberg Byen
strings.d5.s0.tips: Former brewery district with the Elephant Gate and Home of Carlsberg (visitor centre 130 DKK).
strings.d5.s1.name: Frederiksberg Gardens
strings.d5.s1.tips: Romantic park and palace. Take a canal boat, and you can spot the zoo's elephants.
strings.d5.s2.name: Værnedamsvej
strings.d5.s2.tips: The 'Little Paris' street: granola brunch, a cheesemonger and a wine shop.
strings.d5.s3.name: Kødbyen Meatpacking
strings.d5.s3.tips: The White Meatpacking District, with galleries and evening bars.
strings.d5.s4.name: Warpigs Kødbyen
strings.d5.s4.tips: Mikkeller x Three Floyds beer and Texas BBQ.
strings.d5.b0.name: Hija de Sanchez Kødbyen
strings.d5.b1.name: Copenhagen Zoo
strings.d5.b1.tips: Zoo in Frederiksberg with an elephant house by Norman Foster.
strings.d6.s0.name: Assistens Kirkegård
strings.d6.s0.tips: Cemetery-park where Andersen and Kierkegaard are buried, by the yellow wall of Nørrebro.
strings.d6.s1.name: Superkilen Park
strings.d6.s1.tips: BIG's red-and-black multicultural park, with a Moroccan fountain and a Thai boxing ring.
strings.d6.s2.name: Jægersborggade
strings.d6.s2.tips: Nørrebro's hip street: Grød, Meyers Bageri and Coffee Collective.
strings.d6.s3.name: Viking Ship Museum Roskilde
strings.d6.s3.tips: 25 minutes by train. Five original Viking ships and the fjord. In summer (May to September) you can go aboard a ship.
strings.d6.s4.name: Roskilde Cathedral
strings.d6.s4.tips: Burial place of 40 Danish monarchs. UNESCO-listed brick Gothic.
strings.d6.b0.name: Mirabelle Bakery Nørrebro
strings.d6.b1.name: Frederiksborg Castle Hillerød
strings.d6.b1.tips: Renaissance castle on a lake, with the Museum of National History. An alternative to Roskilde.
strings.d7.s0.name: Kastellet
strings.d7.s0.tips: Star-shaped fortress and windmill. Morning joggers.
strings.d7.s1.name: The Little Mermaid
strings.d7.s1.tips: Statue from 1913 at Langelinie. Small and crowded, but a must.
strings.d7.s2.name: Gefion Fountain & St Alban's
strings.d7.s2.tips: Fountain with oxen and the English church.
strings.d7.s3.name: Juno the Bakery Østerbro
strings.d7.s3.tips: The city's best bakery. Try the kardemommebolle (cardamom bun) with a farewell coffee.
strings.d7.s4.name: Østerport Metro Airport
strings.d7.s4.tips: Metro or train to Kastrup takes 15 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Andersen Bakery Østerbro
strings.d7.b1.name: Nyboder
strings.d7.b1.tips: Yellow sailors' houses. An alternative to the fountain.
strings.note0: The Copenhagen Card (72 hours, 889 DKK) covers transport and museums, including Louisiana, Kronborg and Roskilde, and pays for itself on this plan. Bikes cost 100-150 per day and the city is flat. The metro to the airport takes 15 minutes.
strings.note1: Winter is 0-5°C and dark by 16:00. For hygge: Tivoli at Christmas (November to December), Louisiana and cafes. Reffen is closed. Cherry blossom at Bispebjerg in April and May.
strings.note2: Coffee is 45 DKK, smørrebrød 90-150, a restaurant meal 250-400 and a beer 60. No tipping. Cards are accepted everywhere (no cash needed).
strings.note3: Nordic cuisine: Noma has closed, but there are Geranium and Alchemist. Budget options: Hija de Sanchez, Gasoline Grill burgers, and the Juno and Hart bakeries.
strings.note4: Follow the photo rule in Christiania (none on a green light). Pusher Street is closed. Don't walk in the bike lane (cyclists will ring their bells).
strings.note5: Kronborg and Louisiana are covered by the Copenhagen Card. Tivoli's lights come on after 17:00 in the evening.
strings.transit.name: Copenhagen Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: 80+ museums plus all public transport (including Louisiana, Kronborg and Roskilde). 3 days for 889 DKK.
